title: Efficient classical simulation of two-dimensional long-range systems: Rydberg arrays and beyond
authors: Jia-Lin Chan, Tao Xiang, Yantao Wu
abstract: In variational Monte Carlo (VMC) calculations of $N$-site quantum systems with arbitrary all-to-all two-body interactions, evaluating the local energy generally costs $O(N^3)$. We introduce a new framework that reduces this cost to $O(N)$ for tensor network states, capable of scalable and accurate computation of real-time dynamics and ground states. As a result, we obtain accurate simulations of the adiabatic real-time protocol of a $10\times10$ dipolar XY model realized in a Rydberg simulator [C. Chen et al., Nature 616, 691 (2023)], which was previously beyond the reach of classical simulation. Going beyond quantum experiments, we also directly perform ground state VMC to compare with the adiabatic state preparation. Our work demonstrates tensor network VMC as a powerful classical simulator for long-range quantum platforms such as Rydberg and ion-trap simulators, which are currently in urgent need of scalable classical benchmarking tools. As a separate technical contribution, we resolve the pathology of evolving from product states within of tensor network VMC.
summary: The paper presents a novel tensor network Variational Monte Carlo framework that drastically improves the scaling of simulating long-range interacting quantum systems from $O(N^3)$ to $O(N)$. This breakthrough allows for accurate classical simulation of complex dynamics, such as those found in dipolar XY models realized with Rydberg atoms. It establishes a powerful tool for benchmarking future quantum hardware.
main_problem: Developing an efficient classical simulation method for two-dimensional quantum systems with long-range interactions, particularly those relevant to Rydberg arrays and ion traps.
main_result: The authors developed a tensor network VMC framework that reduces the computational cost of local energy evaluation from $O(N^3)$ to $O(N)$, enabling accurate simulation of previously intractable dynamics for systems like the dipolar XY model on a $10 	imes 10$ lattice.
method: The core method is an efficient tensor-network time-dependent Variational Monte Carlo (tVMC) framework utilizing an adaptive basis approach to scale calculations from cubic to linear complexity with system size N.
model_or_system: The study focuses on two-dimensional long-range interacting quantum systems, exemplified by the dipolar XY model ($H_{XY} \propto 1/r^3$) realized in Rydberg simulators. The simulation tracks time evolution under a time-dependent Hamiltonian $H(t) = H_{XY} + H_Z(t)$.
key_observables: Local energy, sublattice magnetization (Z), nearest-neighbor and next-nearest-neighbor correlations ($C_x$, etc.), and squared staggered magnetization ($m_{2\alpha}$).
important_parameters: Long-range interaction decay ($\propto 1/r^3$), lattice size ($10 	imes 10$ for main results), and the time evolution parameter $\delta(t)$.
main_assumptions: The efficiency gain relies on an adaptive basis approach, which trades the zero-variance principle of fixed-basis VMC for computational tractability. For initial steps, Projected tVMC (p-tVMC) is used.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate benchmarks comparing TNS-tVMC results against exact solutions for small lattices ($4 	imes 4$), showing the time evolution of energy and correlations; larger simulations ($10 	imes 10$) confirm long-range correlation maintenance during adiabatic protocols.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem of simulating long-range interactions, details the novel tensor network tVMC framework achieving $O(N)$ scaling via adaptive bases, applies this to simulate the adiabatic real-time protocol for a dipolar XY model in Rydberg arrays, and concludes by benchmarking its accuracy against known ground state limits.
why_interesting: This work provides a crucial computational tool—a scalable classical benchmark—for simulating complex quantum dynamics on emerging hardware platforms like Rydberg and ion traps, bridging theory with experimental feasibility.

(a) average energy ⟨HXY ⟩, (b) averaged sublattice magnetization Z, (c) nearest- neighbor (NN) and next-nearest-neighbor (NNN) corre- lations Cx, and (d) squared staggered magnetization m2 x, all as a function of time.

(a) Energy ⟨HXY ⟩, relaxing to- ward the ground-state value (dashed blue line), which is computed by us using ground state VMC. (b) Con- nected spin correlation C(d) as a function of distance d at t = 4.01, 6.01, 8.01, 9.69, compared with the ground state. (c) Real-space correlation C(∆x, ∆y), averaged over all site pairs separated by displacement (∆x, ∆y), at t = 0.01, 4.81, 9.69 and in the ground state.
